critical_code_review_comments: v60.1.156 design is clean: intercept branch is wrapped in try/catch with a `fallthrough` comment, so if PP_TopupComingSoon fails to load for any reason the Shopify flow still works (graceful degradation).
Defense-in-depth amount-guard duplicated in both the intercept branch AND the Shopify branch is correct — it means a future code-removal of one block can't accidentally bypass the whitelist.

Source-aware eyebrow is rendered via data-testid 'topup-cs-eyebrow-b2b' / 'topup-cs-eyebrow-b2c' so it's automation-friendly for future Playwright tests once the PWA is wired into the Emergent preview.

Defensive isolation layer pp-brand-wallet-isolation-v1.js still wraps PP_TopupComingSoon.show — that's harmless and acts as a final amount-guard at the popup boundary. Consider removing in a future cleanup once team confidence in the per-file guards is high (LOW priority).

rca of the issue: User-reported bug RCA: original symptom was B2B users clicking 'Opwaarderen' and perceiving a redirect to a B2C-looking 'binnenkort' popup. Mis-diagnosed in iteration_3 as 'popup must be removed entirely' → v60.1.155 routed both wallets straight to Shopify. User clarified the popup itself was desired (launch hasn't happened, real checkout would be premature); the REAL bug was that the *shared* PP_TopupComingSoon popup had no visual context to distinguish B2B from B2C, so a B2B click felt like landing in B2C territory. Mitigation v60.1.156: (a) restore the intercept in both topup() functions with try/catch and amount-guard upfront; (b) pass an explicit source label ('b2b' / 'b2c') to PP_TopupComingSoon.show; (c) coming-soon module v1.1.0 reads ctx.source and renders a colour-themed eyebrow above the icon ('Merken Campagne Wallet' for b2b, 'Mijn Wallet' for b2c) so the user instantly knows which wallet context the popup belongs to; (d) update the body copy from 'op dit moment nog niet actief' → 'Opwaarderen is pas mogelijk na de officiële lancering' to set a clearer expectation; (e) keep the Shopify-checkout code below the intercept intact so a single block-deletion at launch flips topup live with no other code changes. Cache-bust + sw.js VERSION bumped uniformly to v60.1.156-restore-coming-soon-popup so every end-user gets the new files on next service-worker activation. Verification: 49 pytest assertions all green, ZIP contents match source tree, /api/downloads returns the updated zip.
